phases.name: Preliminary Phase
phases.objectives: • Establish the architecture capability, its principles, its governance and its tailored framework.  • Confirm which organisations the architecture effort covers, and which it does not.  • Establish the regulatory obligations the architecture must satisfy before any design begins.
phases.inputs: Board strategy — Meridian 2030  ·  Regulatory publications and supervisory correspondence  ·  Existing organisational descriptions  ·  Prior programme post-implementation reviews

phases.name: Phase A: Architecture Vision
phases.objectives: • Establish the scope, constraints and expectations for an architecture cycle.  • Secure approval to proceed, and identify the conduct and prudential exposure the change carries.
phases.inputs: Request for Architecture Work  ·  Architecture Principles  ·  Business Capability Map  ·  Strategic and Motivation Model  ·  Regulatory Obligation Register

phases.name: Phase B: Business Architecture
phases.objectives: • Describe the baseline and target business architecture, and the gap between them.  • Make the insurance operating model explicit: products, channels, underwriting, claims and the actuarial function.
phases.inputs: Architecture Vision  ·  Statement of Architecture Work  ·  Business Capability Map  ·  Organisation Map and Organisation Chart  ·  Business Model Canvas

phases.name: Phase C: Data Architecture
phases.objectives: • Describe the baseline and target data architecture and its authoritative sources.  • Establish the lineage that POPIA, IFRS 17 and the conduct regime each require.
phases.inputs: Business Architecture  ·  Data classification standard STD-07  ·  Regulatory Obligation Register

phases.name: Phase C: Application Architecture
phases.objectives: • Describe the baseline and target application architecture and the rationalisation between them.  • Contain the legacy platform rather than plan a third replacement of it.
phases.inputs: Business Architecture  ·  Data Architecture  ·  Application portfolio catalogue  ·  Technology standards catalogue

phases.name: Phase D: Technology Architecture
phases.objectives: • Describe the baseline and target technology architecture.  • Establish resilience tiering and data placement to the standard the Joint Standards require.
phases.inputs: Application Architecture  ·  Technology standards catalogue STD-01 to STD-16  ·  Resilience standard STD-10  ·  Vendor roadmaps

phases.name: Phase E: Opportunities and Solutions
phases.objectives: • Consolidate the gaps from Phases B to D into work packages and Transition Architectures.  • Sequence against dependency and against what the organisation will actually absorb.
phases.inputs: Gap registers from Phases B, C and D  ·  Business Capability Map  ·  Change history  ·  Run-to-change spend position

phases.name: Phase F: Migration Planning
phases.objectives: • Finalise the Implementation and Migration Plan and confirm it against the delivery portfolio.  • Align the plan to the regulatory calendar, which does not move.
phases.inputs: Architecture Roadmap  ·  Transition Architectures  ·  Regulatory calendar  ·  Portfolio and budget position

phases.name: Phase G: Implementation Governance
phases.objectives: • Ensure that what gets built conforms to the architecture, or carries a recorded dispensation.  • Make the conformance opinion available at each gate without becoming the reason the gate slips.
phases.inputs: Architecture Contracts  ·  Solution designs  ·  Architecture Principles and Standards  ·  Dispensation register

phases.name: Phase H: Architecture Change Management
phases.objectives: • Detect change to the architecture, classify it, and decide whether it is governed.  • Keep the baseline describing the estate that actually exists.
phases.inputs: Repository baseline and current state  ·  Change log  ·  Dispensation register  ·  Post-implementation reviews

phases.name: Requirements Management
phases.objectives: • Manage architecture requirements through the cycle, in both directions.  • Trace every regulatory obligation to the architecture that satisfies it.
phases.inputs: All phases  ·  Regulatory Obligation Register  ·  Architecture Repository

steps.name: Scope the enterprise organizations impacted
steps.note: Four categories recorded: Core, Soft, Extended and Communities.

steps.name: Confirm governance and support frameworks
steps.note: Extended to name the supervisory bodies. Governance at Meridian answers to the Prudential Authority and the FSCA as well as to the Board.

steps.name: Define and establish the enterprise architecture team and organization
steps.note: Produces the Organization Model for Enterprise Architecture.

steps.name: Identify and establish architecture principles
steps.note: Precedence tiers added. TOGAF principles carry no ordering; without one, every conflict is argued from scratch.

steps.name: Tailor TOGAF and other selected frameworks
steps.note: This document.

steps.name: Develop a strategy and implementation plan for tools and techniques
steps.note: Reduced to the repository and the comparison tool. A fourteen-person capability cannot run a tool estate.

steps.name: Establish the regulatory obligation register
steps.note: Every obligation from COFI, POPIA, FICA, IFRS 17 and the Joint Standards, mapped to an accountable owner and to the architecture that satisfies it. TOGAF has no equivalent step and an insurer cannot begin without one.

steps.name: Set the materiality triage
steps.note: Defines what depth of architecture applies to what size of change. Without it, a fourteen-person capability either reviews everything badly or is routed around.

steps.name: Identify stakeholders, concerns and business requirements
steps.note: Uses the stakeholder map from the Strategic and Motivation Model.

steps.name: Confirm and elaborate business goals, drivers and constraints
Evaluate capabilities
steps.note: Uses the four-level capability map rather than a separate Capability Assessment. Differentiation, not maturity, drives the build-versus-buy view.

steps.name: Assess readiness for business transformation
steps.note: Change appetite is an explicit factor, weighted by the 2016 and 2021 programme failures.

steps.name: Define target architecture value propositions and KPIs
Identify business transformation risks and mitigation activities
Develop Statement of Architecture Work and secure approval
Screen conduct and prudential exposure
steps.note: Assesses at vision stage whether the change affects fair customer outcomes, solvency position or a regulatory return. A conduct exposure found in Phase G costs an order of magnitude more than one found here.

steps.name: Confirm capital and solvency impact
steps.note: Whether the change alters the solvency capital requirement or the reserving basis. Consulted with Group Actuarial before the Statement of Architecture Work is signed.

steps.name: Select reference models, views and tools
steps.note: The insurance reference model is Meridian's own capability map rather than an industry model. No SA composite insurer reference model was found that survived contact with the funeral book.

steps.name: Resolve impacts across the Architecture Landscape
Model the product lifecycle
steps.note: From concept through pricing, configuration, launch, in-force management and run-off. Product is the insurer's unit of value and TOGAF has no lifecycle for it.

steps.name: Describe the intermediary and channel model
steps.note: Tied agency, brokers, bancassurance, direct and embedded. Distribution economics differ per channel and drive most business-architecture decisions.

steps.name: Map the actuarial control cycle
steps.note: Pricing, experience analysis, assumption setting and reserving. It runs on a different clock to everything else and constrains what product change is possible when.

steps.name: Select reference models, views and tools
Resolve impacts across the Architecture Landscape
Designate the authoritative source for every entity
steps.note: One system of record per entity, designated by the Data Governance Council. Meridian holds four customer masters; without designation, target architecture is opinion.

steps.name: Establish regulatory data lineage
steps.note: Every figure in a prudential or conduct return traced to its source. IFRS 17 and the Joint Standards both require it and the current process is spreadsheet-based.

steps.name: Classify personal data and attach lawful purpose
steps.note: POPIA requires purpose to travel with the data. It cannot be retrofitted at reporting time.

steps.name: Select reference models, views and tools
Resolve impacts across the Architecture Landscape
Assess policy administration containment
steps.note: For each capability on the legacy platform: wrap, move or leave. Two failed replacements make containment the default and replacement the exception requiring argument.

steps.name: Assess interface managed status
steps.note: Every interface catalogued, owned and authenticated. Forty-four of Meridian's fifty are unmanaged and four read another application's database directly.

steps.name: Select reference models, views and tools
Resolve impacts across the Architecture Landscape
Assign resilience tier and prove recovery
steps.note: Joint Standard 2 of 2024 expects tested recovery, not documented recovery. Meridian has tested 41% of Tier 1 capabilities.

steps.name: Confirm data placement and sovereignty
steps.note: Cloud placement against POPIA and the in-country requirement. A placement decision made at deployment is made too late.

steps.name: Check technology currency against support dates
steps.note: Three components reach end of support during 2027. Currency is an architecture concern, not only an operations one.

steps.name: Determine and confirm key corporate change attributes
Determine business constraints for implementation
steps.note: Change appetite is a named constraint with a stated bound, not a soft factor.

steps.name: Review and consolidate gap analysis results from Phases B to D
Review consolidated requirements across related business functions
Refine and validate dependencies
steps.note: Capability dependency is the primary sequencing input. Wave 2 does not start before the platform Wave 1 delivers.

steps.name: Confirm readiness and risk for business transformation
Formulate the Implementation and Migration Strategy
Identify and group major work packages
Identify Transition Architectures
steps.note: Mandatory rather than optional. Two failed core replacements are two attempts to move without transition states.

steps.name: Create the Architecture Roadmap and Implementation and Migration Plan
Bound the increment against change appetite
steps.note: Each work package is sized against what the organisation has previously absorbed. A package larger than the 2021 attempt requires Board argument, not architecture argument.

steps.name: Assign a business value to each work package
steps.note: Value is stated against a capability movement and a measure, not as a narrative benefit.

steps.name: Estimate resource requirements, project timings and availability
Prioritise migration projects through cost/benefit and risk validation
Confirm Architecture Roadmap and update the Architecture Definition Document
Complete the Implementation and Migration Plan
Complete the architecture development cycle and document lessons learned
Align to the regulatory calendar
steps.note: COFI transition, IFRS 17 reporting cycles and Joint Standard deadlines are fixed. A plan that treats them as negotiable is not a plan.

steps.name: Confirm funding source per work package
steps.note: Every package names where its funding comes from. With no budget increase before FY2028, a package with no named source is not scheduled.

steps.name: Confirm scope and priorities for deployment
Guide development of solutions deployment
steps.note: Depth set by materiality. At Materiality 3 architecture does not guide; it publishes a checklist.

steps.name: Perform enterprise architecture compliance reviews
steps.note: Replaced by the gate model: G1 to G5, with a stated question, evidence and decider at each.

steps.name: Perform post-implementation review and close the implementation
steps.note: Extended to require the baseline architecture be updated to what was actually built, whether or not it matches the design.

steps.name: Triage every engagement by materiality
steps.note: Within five working days. At Materiality 3, no response means deemed approved.

steps.name: Record every significant decision
steps.note: As an Architecture Decision Record with the rejected alternative. Decisions not recorded are relitigated by the next initiative.

steps.name: Deploy monitoring tools
steps.note: The monitoring instrument is the architecture comparison tool, run against the repository rather than against the estate.

steps.name: Provide analysis for architecture change management
steps.note: Every difference classified as design delta, governed drift or ungoverned change. TOGAF distinguishes simplification, incremental and re-architecting change; that classification says nothing about whether the change was authorised.

steps.name: Develop change requirements to meet performance targets
Activate the process to implement change
Detect ungoverned change
steps.note: Difference between two repository states with no change-log entry explaining it. This is the step that catches drift, and TOGAF has no equivalent.

steps.name: Expire and escalate dispensations
steps.note: An expired dispensation reaches the Architecture Board naming the accepting executive.

steps.name: Identify changed requirements and record priorities
Implement requirements arising from Phase H
Implement change in the current phase
Assess and revise gap analysis for past phases
Trace every regulatory obligation to a requirement
steps.note: An obligation with no requirement behind it is an obligation nobody has architected for. Reported to the Risk Committee quarterly.

templates.name: Statement of Architecture Work
templates.purpose: The agreement to do a piece of architecture work. Nothing starts without it.

templates.name: Architecture Vision
templates.purpose: The target state in a form an executive will read. Ten pages maximum.

templates.name: Conduct and Prudential Exposure Screen
templates.purpose: Determines at vision stage whether the change touches fair customer outcomes, solvency or a regulatory return.
templates.approved_by: Chief Compliance Officer; Chief Actuary where capital is engaged
templates.when: Phase A, before the Statement of Architecture Work is signed

templates.name: Business Architecture Definition
templates.purpose: The business architecture: baseline, target and the gap.

templates.name: Product Architecture
templates.purpose: How a product is structured, priced, configured and retired. The insurer's unit of value.

templates.name: Data Architecture Definition
templates.purpose: The data architecture, its authoritative sources and its regulatory lineage.

templates.name: Application Architecture Definition
templates.purpose: The application architecture, portfolio disposition and interface position.

templates.name: Technology Architecture Definition
templates.purpose: The technology architecture, resilience tiering and data placement.

templates.name: Gap Analysis Record
templates.purpose: One record per gap. The instrument that connects a phase to the roadmap.

templates.name: Architecture Roadmap
templates.purpose: Work packages sequenced into waves against dependency and change appetite.

templates.name: Transition Architecture Definition
templates.purpose: A state the enterprise can actually stop at. Mandatory at every wave boundary.

templates.name: Implementation and Migration Plan
templates.purpose: The plan, aligned to the regulatory calendar and to a named funding source per package.

templates.name: Architecture Requirements Specification
templates.purpose: The requirements the architecture must satisfy, with regulatory traceability.

templates.name: Regulatory Obligation Register Entry
templates.purpose: One entry per obligation. The register the architecture is measured against.

templates.name: Lessons Learned Record
templates.purpose: What the cycle taught, recorded while it is still true.
templates.when: Phase F close and Phase H
